title: Levels of architecture: application, solution and enterprise

videos.script: The word architecture covers three different jobs. {{title}} People argue about what an architect does, and very often they mean different jobs. This lesson separates them by scope. {{axes}} Application architecture is the inside of one system. At Carreto, that is how Pricing makes sure no quote leaves below the legal freight floor. The team that builds it decides. {{pricing}} Solution architecture is one outcome across several systems. Carreto wants to pay drivers within twenty-four hours of a delivery. Four teams and a bank are involved, and nobody owns the gap between them. {{payout}} Renata turns that sentence into a time budget, step by step, with an owner for each step. {{budget}} Enterprise architecture is the whole portfolio. Which systems the company should have at all, and what every team shares. {{map}} Renata's first capability map finds the electronic waybill issued from two places, and only one team knew. None of these levels outranks the others. They look different distances ahead, and different people read what they produce. {{table}} By the end, you should be able to take any question and say which level it belongs to. That decides who answers it.
